# Gate Packet: Failure Criteria

Status: DRAFT, thresholds proposed, not ratified by sponsor (Geoffrey Cooper Jr.)
Author: Claude (scrutiny / gate-packet)

## Purpose
These criteria state what evidence would show the Cohabitation Project is not working.
Meeting any single **critical** criterion triggers a mandatory gate review with a
stop / restructure / continue decision. Meeting **three or more** of any severity
triggers the same review.

## Assumptions to verify (not yet checked against source documents)
- T0 = 2026-10-28 (date of the direction document). Correct this if the project clock started elsewhere.
- [TODO] Reconcile with the project's stated failure condition in
  `council/direction-2026-10-28.md`. If it is stricter than the criteria below, the stricter one governs.
- [TODO] Reconcile metric definitions with `council/decisions.md`. Where it defines
  a metric differently, use that definition and note the change here.
- Dollar figures below are placeholders. Replace them with the actual budget.

## Measurement rules
- Agent counts are never evidence of success. Agents are cheap to instantiate, so
  any participation metric that counts agent instances can be inflated at near-zero cost.
  Participation is measured by distinct humans and by human-verified contributions.
- "External" means a person or organization outside the project team, the sponsor's
  organization, and anyone compensated by the project.
- Every metric must be reproducible from logged artifacts (repo history, decision
  log, invoices). Self-reported claims don't count.
- Evidence is collected by someone other than the section authors.

---

## 1. Participation

**1.1 (critical) Human participation floor.**
Fewer than **5 distinct humans** (excluding the sponsor) have made at least one
substantive contribution (reviewed, edited, or authored content that was merged or
logged) by **T0+90 days (2027-01-26)**, or fewer than **3** in any trailing 30-day
window after that.

**1.2 Human retention.**
Fewer than **50%** of humans active in days 1–30 are still active in days 61–90.

**1.3 Human-touch ratio.**
Fewer than **60%** of artifacts shipped in any 30-day window after T0+60 have a
named human reviewer's recorded sign-off. A pipeline that is mostly agents talking
to agents counts as failing, regardless of volume.

**1.4 Agent-inflation flag.**
If agent-instance counts or agent-generated volume are cited as participation
evidence in any gate document without a matching human metric, that document is
invalid for gate purposes. This is a process failure, not a success.

## 2. External uptake of artifacts

**2.1 (critical) Unsolicited external use.**
Fewer than **3 distinct external parties** have used, adopted, cited, or built on a
project artifact, verifiable by link, reply, or fork, by **T0+120 days (2027-02-25)**.
Uptake prompted by direct personal outreach from the team counts only if the
party then acts without further prompting.

**2.2 Inbound signal.**
Zero externally originated issues, pull requests, questions, or requests by **T0+90 days**.

**2.3 No repeat use.**
Of external parties who used an artifact once, fewer than **1** returns for a
second, separate use by **T0+180 days (2027-04-26)**.

**2.4 Vanity-metric exclusion.**
Page views, downloads, stars, and impressions are reported but do not count
toward 2.1–2.3.

## 3. Section output quality

**3.1 (critical) Blind review pass rate.**
In a blind review by at least **2 reviewers not involved in producing the section**
against a pre-published rubric, fewer than **60% of sampled sections** (sample of at
least 10, or all if fewer, drawn randomly) pass, in either of the first two
review rounds (**T0+60** and **T0+120**).

**3.2 Baseline comparison.**
In blind pairwise comparison against a single-agent, single-pass baseline on the
same brief, the cohabitation output is preferred in fewer than **60%** of
comparisons (sample of at least 10). If the multi-party process isn't beating
a single prompt, the structure is not adding value.

**3.3 Factual error rate.**
Spot-checks of at least 10 sections find a verifiable factual or citation error in
more than **25%** of them.

**3.4 Rework rate.**
More than **40%** of sections shipped in a 30-day window are materially revised or
retracted within 30 days of shipping.

**3.5 Throughput.**
Fewer than **[N, from direction doc]** sections accepted by T0+120 days.

## 4. Governance functioning

**4.1 (critical) Decision record integrity.**
In a sample of at least 10 decisions (or all, if fewer) from `council/decisions.md`
at T0+90, fewer than **80%** have a recorded owner, rationale, and date. Any decision
found to have been made and enforced without a log entry counts as a separate violation.

**4.2 Decision latency.**
The median time from an item being raised to a logged decision exceeds **14 days**
over any 60-day period.

**4.3 Scrutiny findings addressed.**
More than **30%** of scrutiny findings rated high severity remain without a
logged response after **30 days**.

**4.4 Scope and authority breaches.**
**2 or more** confirmed instances in a 60-day window of an agent or team acting
outside its delegated scope, or of the sponsor's approval being claimed without
a record of it.

**4.5 Direction thrash.**
More than **2** changes to the stated direction or success metrics within any
60-day window without a logged evidence-based rationale. Moving the goalposts
counts as governance failure.

**4.6 Criteria drift.**
Any change to this document after T0+30 without a dated entry in `decisions.md`
invalidates the change.

## 5. Financial sustainability

**5.1 (critical) Runway.**
Committed funding covers fewer than **90 days** of projected burn at any point after
**T0+90 days**, with no signed or documented commitment to extend.

**5.2 Cost per accepted section.**
Total spend (compute, tooling, human time at a stated rate) divided by sections
passing 3.1 exceeds **[$X, set by sponsor]** over any 60-day period, or is rising
for 3 consecutive months.

**5.3 Budget overrun.**
Actual spend exceeds budget by more than **25%** in any month or by **15%**
cumulatively.

**5.4 Revenue / external funding.**
By **T0+180 days**, external revenue, grants, or committed third-party funding is
under **[$Y]**, or under **[Z%]** of spend. [TODO: replace with the project's
actual sustainability model.]

**5.5 Hidden subsidy.**
If more than **30%** of the costs depend on unpaid or unlogged sponsor
contribution, report it and treat 5.1 as if that contribution stopped.

---

## Review protocol
- Checks run at T0+60, T0+90, T0+120, and T0+180 by a reviewer independent of section
  authors.
- Results are logged in `decisions.md` whether or not any criterion triggers.
- A triggered critical criterion cannot be dismissed without a written, dated
  sponsor decision that names the criterion and the reason.

## Known limits
- Small sample sizes mean borderline results are noisy. If a result is within 10%
  of a threshold, re-sample before acting.
- These criteria detect failure, not success. Passing all of them is necessary
  but not sufficient.
